entries.description: The replay buffer at size, attempt 1: 8,000 prompts self-distilled greedily from the instruct checkpoint, the hard prerequisite for arms C5a and C5b.
entries.note: FAILED on 1 assertion, and the assertion was right. The generation itself was clean and is not the problem: 7,945 of 8,000 sampled prompts usable inside the 1,024-token cap, 7,945 completions, 0 empty, 1,850,696 completion tokens at 1,688.5 tok/s, file placed in shared storage. The n_tok count written into each row came back as exactly 2 for every row (15,890 total), because row_tokens called apply_chat_template(tokenize=True) and took len() of the result, which on this transformers version is a BatchEncoding whose len() is its KEY COUNT (input_ids, attention_mask) rather than its token count. That is precisely the silent defect this generator was rewritten at 17:09Z to prevent, arriving through a different door. The downstream C5b ratio check caught it (a 3.2M-token dose over a 0.02M-token buffer reads as 201.4 passes, over the 2.0 ceiling), so no arm ever trained on it. Fixed and re-uploaded: _ids() now unwraps BatchEncoding/dict/batched forms before counting, an exact invariant was added (training tokens can never fall below the completion tokens the rows were built from, which this run violated by two orders of magnitude and which names the cause directly instead of leaving it to be inferred from a replay-passes number), and an 8-case fixture test covers every return shape plus the len()==2 regression itself. Requeue when a slot frees; C5a and C5b are last in the arm order, so nothing is blocked yet. Spend recorded because the GPU time was really consumed.

entries.note: Completed clean: 8416/8416 steps, 65,576,421 tokens seen at 6094.3 tok/s over 3.001 GPU-h (aggregate incl. supervisor overhead), val_loss 0.1517 (delta -1.1035 from the base checkpoint), 0 assertion failures, peak 6.07 GB on a 47.7 GB card. entries.label: Pack A -- arms C3 (full-parameter), C7 (raw mix), C2p (no guardrail block) on one L40S
entries.note: 3/3 arms exited rc=0 at the full 64.0M-token budget, 0 assertion failures, 18 per-arm artifacts plus pack_summary.json all verified present. val_loss C2p 0.1511, C3 0.1513, C7 0.1565. The charge is card-hours, not the sum of the three arms' own gpu_hours (8.066+9.167+8.983=26.2), which is the whole point of packing: three arms cost one card's wall clock.

entries.label: Packed evaluation smoke, first attempt -- failed on a config round-trip before any scoring ran
entries.note: The supervisor rejected its own valid input. `-p pack_overrides='{...}'` is typed on the way in, so job_data stores a dict; pack.py did str() on it and got a Python repr, which is not JSON. Patched to accept a mapping as-is (and a repr as a fallback), with both shapes added to the scheduling contract test, and re-queued as 37b50115. Charged for the launch, not for work.

entries.label: Packed evaluation smoke, re-queue -- arms E1 (bfcl,probes) and E2 (ifstruct,ifeval), 16 items each on one L4
entries.note: 2/2 arms exited rc=0, 0 assertion failures, 19 artifacts. Four components split across two arms on one L4: E1 (bfcl, probes) 142.6 s, E2 (ifstruct, ifeval) 79.9 s, total wall 151 s, so the two ran concurrently rather than in sequence. The packed scoring path is proven end to end.

entries.label: Four-arm loadability and sizing smoke -- C1, C2p, C3, C7 at 16 items a component on one L4
entries.note: Answered both questions it was queued for and failed on a third. All four arms ran out of memory on their first BFCL batch under 5.2 GB ceilings: 4.41 GB allocated, 772 MB more wanted, and C7 was killed with 17.33 GB of the card still free, so the per-arm ceiling ended it rather than contention. Banked regardless: C3's full-parameter checkpoint loads as a model rather than as an adapter, and all four adapters resolve out of storage after the manual move. Scoring holds a little over 5.2 GB an arm at batch 16, which is two arms an L4 and not four; prefill carries the batch times the sequence length and BFCL's tool schemas run to about 3k tokens.
